Good digital work does more than look good. It earns trust, works for everyone and speaks your customers' language.

A website is often the first conversation a customer has with your business. It should look considered, load quickly, work on every screen, treat visitors' data with respect — and read naturally in their language.

That is why we bring design, development, digital compliance and translation into one process. The result is a website that makes your business more credible, more accessible and ready for customers across Europe.

Digital compliance

Design and compliance belong in the same conversation.

Cookie banners, contact forms and privacy notices are part of the user experience. We help you understand which European rules may apply to your website — and build them in properly, rather than adding them at the end.

Explore digital compliance

General information, not legal advice. Whether a rule applies depends on your business, your website and your country. For advice on your situation, consult a qualified lawyer.

Applies to most business websites

04

Personal data & the GDPR

Applies whenever a website processes personal data — contact forms, newsletter sign-ups, analytics, even server logs.

Regulation (EU) 2016/679

Cookie consent & tracking

Non-essential cookies and similar tracking generally need prior consent. Strictly necessary storage does not.

Directive 2002/58/EC, Art. 5(3)

Privacy notices

Visitors must be told who processes their data, why, on what legal basis, and what their rights are.

GDPR Art. 13–14

Forms & data collection

Collect only what you need, protect it in transit and decide how long you keep it.

GDPR Art. 5, 25, 32

Depends on your business

04

Provider information

Commercial websites must identify the provider. Germany and Austria have specific, detailed legal-notice (Impressum) rules.

Directive 2000/31/EC, Art. 5 · DE: § 5 DDG

Digital accessibility

The European Accessibility Act covers certain products and services, such as e-commerce, since June 2025. Microenterprises providing services are exempt.

Directive (EU) 2019/882

Digital Services Act

Relevant if you host user content or run an online platform or marketplace. A typical company website is usually not affected.

Regulation (EU) 2022/2065

EU AI Act

Relevant if you develop or use AI systems, such as chatbots or AI-generated content. Obligations apply in phases; several dates were moved in 2026.

Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by (EU) 2026/1744

Good practice

02

Accessible design

Readable contrast, keyboard navigation and clear structure help every visitor — even where not legally required.

WCAG 2.2, level AA

Privacy by default

No unnecessary trackers, self-hosted fonts and honest consent choices with equal Accept and Reject options.

Lexora standard

Last reviewed October 2026 · sources: EUR-Lex

Our approach

A clear process, without surprises.

Every project follows the same four steps, with a defined scope and an agreed price before work begins.

  1. 01

    Discover

    We get to know your business, your audience and your goals — and agree on what the project includes.

  2. 02

    Design

    We develop a considered visual direction and page structure, and refine it with your feedback.

  3. 03

    Build

    We develop the website, test it on real devices and browsers, and fix what needs fixing.

  4. 04

    Launch

    We deploy the site and hand over clear information on how it works and what comes next.
